name: go2_stand
title: Go2 stand (deterministic hold on the nominal stance -- NO learned policy)
summary: The second specialist a quadruped BATON sequence needs, and the cheapest skill in the library: a Go2 standing is a DETERMINISTIC HOLD on its nominal stance. Four feet on the ground is statically stable, so the specialist that holds it needs no policy at all -- in BATON it is registered with an empty checkpoint (policy=None), contributes a ZERO residual, and tracks its ghost exactly. Contrast the G1's stand_rl, which is a *trained* specialist riding a weight-bearing crane: a biped is not statically stable, and that difference is precisely what a policy-switching LIBRARY must not care about.

ghost.format: json lut (nb=64 bins, 12 joints, constant leg track, vx=0, zero feedforward)
ghost.provenance: constructed-feasible: the Go2's OWN gait model standing_pose(body_height=0.30) held constant over 64 bins. Not designed, not recorded -- READ from the model the deploy already uses. Achievable by construction: it is the pose the robot settles into under its deploy PD before the gait clock ever starts.
ghost.validator: WARN (stamped into the lut, 2026-07-13). All model-aware gates PASS against the REAL go2.urdf (T0.model-coverage, position-limits, velocity-limits) and provenance is constructed-feasible. The single WARN is T0.leg-symmetry, which is a CATEGORY ARTIFACT, not a defect: it correlates a phase-mirrored waveform, and a constant hold has zero variance, so the correlation is undefined (amp ratio 0.00). The G1's own stand ghost (ghost_stand_v1) stamps WARN for exactly the same reason. The honest fix is to make the cyclic gates n/a for motion_class=static, as they already are for sequence -- not to massage this ghost.
ghost.shape_parity: SAME robot, SAME joint names/order, SAME nb=64 as go2_shadow_ghost_lut.json -- REQUIRED, because BATON blends the two element-wise.

baton.specialist_entry: stand||<lut>|0   (the EMPTY checkpoint field is what makes it a hold)
baton.notes: A legal BATON leg with no policy behind it. This is what let the quadruped BATON demo exist without training anything.

deploy.notes: Runs as the `stand` leg of the walk -> stand -> walk BATON sequence. The world is IDENTICAL in scene and physics to go2_shadow_deploy.omniworld; only the controller line differs.

verification.result: See the go2_baton demo. Offline (no engine): the settled hold applies EXACTLY zero residual and tracks the stance ghost exactly; the morph crossfades over BATON_MORPH_TICKS.
honest_caveats: This is a HOLD, not a balance controller. It does not reject pushes, it does not recover from a shove -- it commands the nominal stance and a statically stable quadruped stays up. Do not describe it as push-recovery.
It is only 'verified' as a BATON leg (the handover works and the robot does not fall). It has not been exam'd standalone under disturbance.
